Read text file `AGENTS.md`.
1|# AGENTS.md — how a book becomes software and skills in this repo
2|
3|This file is the book-agnostic playbook. It applies to every book under `books/`. Nothing here is
4|specific to one book; the worked example is `books/release-it/` (start with its `PLAN.md`).
5|Repo-wide agent rules from `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (seats, fresh-agent lifecycle, cross-family
6|review, commit style) still apply; this file only adds what is particular to breaking down a book.
7|
8|## Purpose
9|
10|Nick reads a technical book. The repo turns it into two artifacts:
11|
12|1. **One flawed archetype project per book, improved lesson by lesson.** A single realistic
13|   service or program, built with real technology and seeded with deliberate, realistic flaws that
14|   the book warns about. Each lesson of the book is a **patch commit** that fixes one flaw (or one
15|   tight cluster) in that same codebase. The commit history is the teaching artifact: the first tag
16|   is the "before", every lesson tag is a checkpoint a reader can run, and the final tag implements
17|   the book's lessons. `git log` reads as the codebase getting better.
18|2. **Skills** that CODIFY the book's main parts as reusable procedures an agent (or a person) can
19|   run on real code and real designs, each pointing at the project as its worked example.
20|
21|The book itself is the source of truth. Every flaw, lesson and skill must trace back to specific
22|chapters.
23|
24|## Phase flow and the confirmation gate
25|
26|| Phase | Seat | Produces | Done when |
27||---|---|---|---|
28|| 1. Research & plan | planner (top tier) | `books/<slug>/PLAN.md` (project design, deliberate-issues register, lesson sequence, skills, build order), `STATE.md` update | **Nick has confirmed the plan.** Nothing is delegated to a builder before that. |
29|| 2. Build v0 + lessons | builder (top tier; the work is subtle concurrency and failure behaviour) | `books/<slug>/project/` at the flawed tag, then one commit per lesson with its note and verify script, tags per plan | Every lesson's verify passes at its tag and reproduces the flaw at the previous tag; checkpoints reviewed |
30|| 3. Write skills | builder (may follow phase 2 directly) | `books/<slug>/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` for each planned skill | Each skill meets the skills contract and cites its chapters and the project |
31|| 4. Review | reviewer from a DIFFERENT model family than the builder | Review notes in `STATE.md`; fixes folded into the lessons they belong to | Review bar below is met; verdict recorded |
32|
33|**The gate.** The planner's plan is a proposal until Nick confirms it. Plan revisions (v1 → v2 → …)
34|are committed as documents; the previous plan is archived next to the new one when the approach
35|changes. Phase 2 may also be split into checkpoints (the plan says which), each confirmed by a
36|cross-family review before the next begins. Builders do not re-decide structure: the register and the
37|lesson order are fixed by the plan; thresholds and sizes may be tuned, with the deviation recorded in
38|the lesson note and in `STATE.md`.
39|
40|Hand-off between phases is through files in the repo, never through chat.
41|
42|## Choosing the archetype project
43|
44|The plan picks one project per book. It earns the role if ALL of these hold:
45|
46|- Every core, transferable idea of the book has a **natural home** in it: a place where the flaw the
47|  book describes would plausibly be written by a competent team, and where its fix is the book's
48|  remedy. If a core idea has no home, the archetype is wrong, not the idea.
49|- It is **modest**: a few thousand lines at the flawed tag, buildable by one builder pass.
50|- It is built on **real technology** for its domain (Docker Compose if it is a service; a real
51|  database; real instrumentation such as Prometheus; a real load balancer or fault injector where the
52|  book's lessons involve them), chosen and justified per component in the plan. One primary language,
53|  chosen by what makes the book's failures and remedies most visible.
54|- It **runs badly, not brokenly**: at the flawed tag it passes its own tests and serves gentle load.
55|  Flaws are behavioural (hangs, storms, unbounded growth, cascades, lost work), never compile errors
56|  or cartoon sabotage, and never marked in the code. The plan's register is the only list of them.
57|
58|## The deliberate-issues register
59|
60|The heart of the plan. One row per flaw: id, where it lives (file / area), how it shows under the
61|right load, the chapter and anti-pattern that names it, and the lesson that fixes it. Flaws must be
62|realistic (the kind real codebases have), individually demonstrable on the tree one lesson before
63|their fix, and fixable in one focused patch each. The register doubles as the answer key for the
64|book's "hunt for X" skill.
65|
66|## Lesson contract
67|
68|A lesson is one commit on the main line (two if the plan says the patch would exceed ~400 lines; the
69|lesson tag points at the last). It contains:
70|
71|1. **The patch**: the fix for the register rows it names and nothing else. A reader must be able to
72|   `git diff <prev-tag> <tag> -- project/` and understand it in minutes.
73|2. **The note** `books/<slug>/lessons/NN-<slug>.md`: the idea in plain words with chapter citations;
74|   the flaw with `file:line` pointers into the previous tag; the patch walkthrough naming the lines
75|   that matter; the verification with the exact command and expected before/after output; "try
76|   changing"; where to read more. Written for someone who has not read the book yet.
77|3. **The verify script** `project/lab/verify/NN-<slug>.sh`, run as `make verify LESSON=NN`: resets
78|   state, applies the load and chaos timeline, prints a comparable report table and the named
79|   metrics, and ends with a verdict line starting `IMPROVED:` or `FLAW REPRODUCED:` against explicit
80|   thresholds. `make verify LESSON=NN REF=<previous tag>` runs the same script with the project built
81|   from the previous tag and must reproduce the flaw. Runs in a couple of minutes with warm images.
82|4. **The commit body**: flaw, fix, both verdict lines pasted in. It must stand alone in `git log`.
83|5. **A tag** per the plan's naming (`<slug>/v0-flawed`, `<slug>/lesson-NN`, `<slug>/v1-hardened`).
84|
85|Chaos is injected only from outside the codebase (fault injector API, container kill/pause/restart,
86|partner-fake admin endpoints, SQL run by the script), never through hidden paths in the service.
87|History may be rewritten (fixups folded into their lesson, tags re-pointed) until Nick accepts the
88|final tag; after that it is frozen.
89|
90|## Layout of a book
91|
92|```
93|books/<slug>/
94|  PLAN.md                     # the confirmed plan; earlier versions archived alongside
95|  README.md                   # landing page: argument, lesson index with tags, skills index
96|  lessons/
97|    README.md                 # index: lesson, tag, flaw ids, verify command
98|    00-<the-flawed-start>.md  # tour of the flawed tag and the register
99|    NN-<lesson>.md            # one note per lesson
100|  project/                    # the one codebase; `make up`, `make verify LESSON=NN`, `make down`
101|    lab/                      # load generator, verify runner and scripts, report queries
102|  skills/
103|    README.md                 # index of the book's skills with triggers
104|    <skill-name>/SKILL.md
105|```
106|
107|Names are stable once committed: notes, skills and commit bodies link to them.
108|
109|## Skills contract
110|
111|A skill is an **actionable procedure**, not a summary of the book. It lives at
112|`books/<slug>/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` in the format that Claude Code and Codex load:
113|
114|```
115|---
116|name: <skill-name>
117|description: <one line: what it does and when to use it — this is what triggers it>
118|---
119|```
120|
121|followed by these sections:
122|
123|- **When to use** — concrete triggers (the kind of code, question, or event that should invoke it).
124|- **Inputs** — what the agent needs at hand (a repo, a design doc, an incident timeline).
125|- **Procedure** — numbered steps an agent can execute, each with what to look for or do, and
126|  concrete signals (grep patterns, questions, thresholds) where the book gives them.
127|- **Output** — the shape of the result (a table, a checklist, a plan) so results are comparable.
128|- **Source** — the chapters the steps come from, and the lessons in this repo that demonstrate them.
129|- **Worked example** — what the skill produces when run against the book's project (for a "hunt"
130|  skill, the register is the answer key and the skill is expected to find most of it).
131|
132|A skill may reference the book's vocabulary but must be usable by someone who has not read it.
133|Skill names are imperative verb phrases (`test-integration-points`, `plan-safe-release`).
134|Aim for 5 to 8 skills per book; each must earn its place by covering a part of the book the others
135|do not.
136|
137|## Review bar
138|
139|The phase-4 reviewer checks, from a FRESH clone on this VM:
140|
141|1. At the flawed tag, the project builds, its tests pass and its baseline verify passes: the flaws
142|   are latent, not obvious.
143|2. For every lesson, `make verify LESSON=NN` passes at its tag and
144|   `make verify LESSON=NN REF=<previous tag>` reproduces the flaw, each within its time budget. The
145|   verdict lines match the commit body.
146|3. Each lesson's diff is confined to what its note claims; no flaw is fixed early by accident and no
147|   new one is introduced (spot-check two later lessons' verify at an earlier tag).
148|4. Every claim about the book in a note, the plan or a skill traces to a chapter or named section
149|   that actually says it. Chapter numbers match the edition named in the plan. Spot-check at least
150|   one citation per lesson and per skill.
151|5. Each skill is executable as a procedure and is not a chapter summary; its worked example matches
152|   the project.
153|6. History is linear, tags are where the plan says, and `git log` reads as the intended story.
154|
155|Verdicts are PASS / NITS / FAIL per the repo-wide protocol; one repair round, then arbitration.
156|
157|## Conventions
158|
159|- Commit subjects `<area>: <imperative summary>`; `<area>` is `docs`, the book slug (`release-it`)
160|  for plan-level and landing-page commits, the project name (`litefleet` for Release It!) for lesson commits, `skills`,
161|  or `repo`. Lesson commits end their subject with `(lesson NN)`.
162|- `STATE.md` at the repo root records which book is in which phase and what is next; update it in
163|  the same commit as the phase's deliverable.
164|- Durable knowledge about this repo's process goes in `docs/knowledge/` (not the `kb` CLI, which is
165|  for VM/environment facts).
166|- Scratch files go in `/tmp/<task>/`, never in the repo. Load-test results under `project/results/`
167|  are gitignored.
168|
169|## Starting a new book
170|
171|1. Create `books/<slug>/` and write `PLAN.md` following `books/release-it/PLAN.md`: core argument →
172|   archetype project (what it does, components, partners, stack with rationale) → deliberate-issues
173|   register → lesson sequence (source, flaw, patch, commit subject, verify) → coverage honesty →
174|   skills → build order and budget → layout → decisions to confirm.
175|2. Add the book to the root `README.md` index and to `STATE.md`. Commit.
176|3. Wait for Nick's confirmation. Then dispatch phase 2 to a builder seat with the plan as the brief,
177|   one checkpoint at a time.

1|# AGENTS.md — how a book becomes software and skills in this repo
2|
3|This file is the book-agnostic playbook. It applies to every book under `books/`. Nothing here is
4|specific to one book; the worked example is `books/release-it/` (start with its `PLAN.md`).
5|Repo-wide agent rules from `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (seats, fresh-agent lifecycle, cross-family
6|review, commit style) still apply; this file only adds what is particular to breaking down a book.
7|
8|## Purpose
9|
10|Nick reads a technical book. The repo turns it into two artifacts:
11|
12|1. **One flawed archetype project per book, improved lesson by lesson.** A single realistic
13|   service or program, built with real technology and seeded with deliberate, realistic flaws that
14|   the book warns about. Each lesson of the book is a **patch commit** that fixes one flaw (or one
15|   tight cluster) in that same codebase. The commit history is the teaching artifact: the first tag
16|   is the "before", every lesson tag is a checkpoint a reader can run, and the final tag implements
17|   the book's lessons. `git log` reads as the codebase getting better.
18|2. **Skills** that CODIFY the book's main parts as reusable procedures an agent (or a person) can
19|   run on real code and real designs, each pointing at the project as its worked example.
20|
21|The book itself is the source of truth. Every flaw, lesson and skill must trace back to specific
22|chapters.
23|
24|## Phase flow and the confirmation gate
25|
26|| Phase | Seat | Produces | Done when |
27||---|---|---|---|
28|| 1. Research & plan | planner (top tier) | `books/<slug>/PLAN.md` (project design, deliberate-issues register, lesson sequence, skills, build order), `STATE.md` update | **Nick has confirmed the plan.** Nothing is delegated to a builder before that. |
29|| 2. Build v0 + lessons | builder (top tier; the work is subtle concurrency and failure behaviour) | `books/<slug>/project/` at the flawed tag, then one commit per lesson with its note and verify script, tags per plan | Every lesson's verify passes at its tag and reproduces the flaw at the previous tag; checkpoints reviewed |
30|| 3. Write skills | builder (may follow phase 2 directly) | `books/<slug>/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` for each planned skill | Each skill meets the skills contract and cites its chapters and the project |
31|| 4. Review | reviewer from a DIFFERENT model family than the builder | Review notes in `STATE.md`; fixes folded into the lessons they belong to | Review bar below is met; verdict recorded |
32|
33|**The gate.** The planner's plan is a proposal until Nick confirms it. Plan revisions (v1 → v2 → …)
34|are committed as documents; the previous plan is archived next to the new one when the approach
35|changes. Phase 2 may also be split into checkpoints (the plan says which), each confirmed by a
36|cross-family review before the next begins. Builders do not re-decide structure: the register and the
37|lesson order are fixed by the plan; thresholds and sizes may be tuned, with the deviation recorded in
38|the lesson note and in `STATE.md`.
39|
40|Hand-off between phases is through files in the repo, never through chat.
41|
42|## Choosing the archetype project
43|
44|The plan picks one project per book. It earns the role if ALL of these hold:
45|
46|- Every core, transferable idea of the book has a **natural home** in it: a place where the flaw the
47|  book describes would plausibly be written by a competent team, and where its fix is the book's
48|  remedy. If a core idea has no home, the archetype is wrong, not the idea.
49|- It is **modest**: a few thousand lines at the flawed tag, buildable by one builder pass.
50|- It is built on **real technology** for its domain (Docker Compose if it is a service; a real
51|  database; real instrumentation such as Prometheus; a real load balancer or fault injector where the
52|  book's lessons involve them), chosen and justified per component in the plan. One primary language,
53|  chosen by what makes the book's failures and remedies most visible.
54|- It **runs badly, not brokenly**: at the flawed tag it passes its own tests and serves gentle load.
55|  Flaws are behavioural (hangs, storms, unbounded growth, cascades, lost work), never compile errors
56|  or cartoon sabotage, and never marked in the code. The plan's register is the only list of them.
57|
58|## The deliberate-issues register
59|
60|The heart of the plan. One row per flaw: id, where it lives (file / area), how it shows under the
61|right load, the chapter and anti-pattern that names it, and the lesson that fixes it. Flaws must be
62|realistic (the kind real codebases have), individually demonstrable on the tree one lesson before
63|their fix, and fixable in one focused patch each. The register doubles as the answer key for the
64|book's "hunt for X" skill.
65|
66|## Lesson contract
67|
68|A lesson is one commit on the main line (two if the plan says the patch would exceed ~400 lines; the
69|lesson tag points at the last). It contains:
70|
71|1. **The patch**: the fix for the register rows it names and nothing else. A reader must be able to
72|   `git diff <prev-tag> <tag> -- project/` and understand it in minutes.
73|2. **The note** `books/<slug>/lessons/NN-<slug>.md`: the idea in plain words with chapter citations;
74|   the flaw with `file:line` pointers into the previous tag; the patch walkthrough naming the lines
75|   that matter; the verification with the exact command and expected before/after output; "try
76|   changing"; where to read more. Written for someone who has not read the book yet.
77|3. **The verify script** `project/lab/verify/NN-<slug>.sh`, run as `make verify LESSON=NN`: resets
78|   state, applies the load and chaos timeline, prints a comparable report table and the named
79|   metrics, and ends with a verdict line starting `IMPROVED:` or `FLAW REPRODUCED:` against explicit
80|   thresholds. `make verify LESSON=NN REF=<previous tag>` runs the same script with the project built
81|   from the previous tag and must reproduce the flaw. Runs in a couple of minutes with warm images.
82|4. **The commit body**: flaw, fix, both verdict lines pasted in. It must stand alone in `git log`.
83|5. **A tag** per the plan's naming (`<slug>/v0-flawed`, `<slug>/lesson-NN`, `<slug>/v1-hardened`).
84|
85|Chaos is injected only from outside the codebase (fault injector API, container kill/pause/restart,
86|partner-fake admin endpoints, SQL run by the script), never through hidden paths in the service.
87|History may be rewritten (fixups folded into their lesson, tags re-pointed) until Nick accepts the
88|final tag; after that it is frozen.
89|
90|## Layout of a book
91|
92|```
93|books/<slug>/
94|  PLAN.md                     # the confirmed plan; earlier versions archived alongside
95|  README.md                   # landing page: argument, lesson index with tags, skills index
96|  lessons/
97|    README.md                 # index: lesson, tag, flaw ids, verify command
98|    00-<the-flawed-start>.md  # tour of the flawed tag and the register
99|    NN-<lesson>.md            # one note per lesson
100|  project/                    # the one codebase; `make up`, `make verify LESSON=NN`, `make down`
101|    lab/                      # load generator, verify runner and scripts, report queries
102|  skills/
103|    README.md                 # index of the book's skills with triggers
104|    <skill-name>/SKILL.md
105|```
106|
107|Names are stable once committed: notes, skills and commit bodies link to them.
108|
109|## Skills contract
110|
111|A skill is an **actionable procedure**, not a summary of the book. It lives at
112|`books/<slug>/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` in the format that Claude Code and Codex load:
113|
114|```
115|---
116|name: <skill-name>
117|description: <one line: what it does and when to use it — this is what triggers it>
118|---
119|```
120|
121|followed by these sections:
122|
123|- **When to use** — concrete triggers (the kind of code, question, or event that should invoke it).
124|- **Inputs** — what the agent needs at hand (a repo, a design doc, an incident timeline).
125|- **Procedure** — numbered steps an agent can execute, each with what to look for or do, and
126|  concrete signals (grep patterns, questions, thresholds) where the book gives them.
127|- **Output** — the shape of the result (a table, a checklist, a plan) so results are comparable.
128|- **Source** — the chapters the steps come from, and the lessons in this repo that demonstrate them.
129|- **Worked example** — what the skill produces when run against the book's project (for a "hunt"
130|  skill, the register is the answer key and the skill is expected to find most of it).
131|
132|A skill may reference the book's vocabulary but must be usable by someone who has not read it.
133|Skill names are imperative verb phrases (`test-integration-points`, `plan-safe-release`).
134|Aim for 5 to 8 skills per book; each must earn its place by covering a part of the book the others
135|do not.
136|
137|## Review bar
138|
139|The phase-4 reviewer checks, from a FRESH clone on this VM:
140|
141|1. At the flawed tag, the project builds, its tests pass and its baseline verify passes: the flaws
142|   are latent, not obvious.
143|2. For every lesson, `make verify LESSON=NN` passes at its tag and
144|   `make verify LESSON=NN REF=<previous tag>` reproduces the flaw, each within its time budget. The
145|   verdict lines match the commit body.
146|3. Each lesson's diff is confined to what its note claims; no flaw is fixed early by accident and no
147|   new one is introduced (spot-check two later lessons' verify at an earlier tag).
148|4. Every claim about the book in a note, the plan or a skill traces to a chapter or named section
149|   that actually says it. Chapter numbers match the edition named in the plan. Spot-check at least
150|   one citation per lesson and per skill.
151|5. Each skill is executable as a procedure and is not a chapter summary; its worked example matches
152|   the project.
153|6. History is linear, tags are where the plan says, and `git log` reads as the intended story.
154|
155|Verdicts are PASS / NITS / FAIL per the repo-wide protocol; one repair round, then arbitration.
156|
157|## Conventions
158|
159|- Commit subjects `<area>: <imperative summary>`; `<area>` is `docs`, the book slug (`release-it`)
160|  for plan-level and landing-page commits, the project name (`litefleet` for Release It!) for lesson commits, `skills`,
161|  or `repo`. Lesson commits end their subject with `(lesson NN)`.
162|- `STATE.md` at the repo root records which book is in which phase and what is next; update it in
163|  the same commit as the phase's deliverable.
164|- Durable knowledge about this repo's process goes in `docs/knowledge/` (not the `kb` CLI, which is
165|  for VM/environment facts).
166|- Scratch files go in `/tmp/<task>/`, never in the repo. Load-test results under `project/results/`
167|  are gitignored.
168|
169|## Starting a new book
170|
171|1. Create `books/<slug>/` and write `PLAN.md` following `books/release-it/PLAN.md`: core argument →
172|   archetype project (what it does, components, partners, stack with rationale) → deliberate-issues
173|   register → lesson sequence (source, flaw, patch, commit subject, verify) → coverage honesty →
174|   skills → build order and budget → layout → decisions to confirm.
175|2. Add the book to the root `README.md` index and to `STATE.md`. Commit.
176|3. Wait for Nick's confirmation. Then dispatch phase 2 to a builder seat with the plan as the brief,
177|   one checkpoint at a time.

1|# Queuelet exploration protocol
2|
3|An experiment teaches us about the inherited system by comparing a prediction with observation. Source reading is allowed and valuable; the register, proof scripts and SUT history are withheld. This document defines the local record and roles. It does not describe expected defects.
4|
5|## Roles and export
6|
7|The coordinator prepares a charter and an empty export directory. The seeder/fixer and explorer must be from different model families. Every experiment uses a fresh headless explorer. The reviewer independently checks the checkpoint and blindness boundary.
8|
9|Export only the previous tag’s `books/explore-it/project`, `books/explore-it/exploration`, `books/explore-it/skills` and `books/explore-it/lessons`, preserving their relative paths. From the repository root, with the chosen tag and an existing empty destination:
10|
11|```sh
12|git archive "$experiment_tag" books/explore-it/project books/explore-it/exploration books/explore-it/skills books/explore-it/lessons | tar -x -C "$export_dir"
13|```
14|
15|The export has no `.git`, `PLAN.md`, `register/`, seeder proofs or hidden copy of repository history. Inspect its file list before dispatch. Existing experiment records, disclosed previous lessons and repro scripts may be present at later tags; they are prior knowledge, never a briefing about unfound targets. Keep the new charter and brief free of planted hints. The explorer can read any file in the export, including all source, and run the lab; it must not read outside the export or consult the originating checkout. Where external tools/services are necessary, their permitted use is specified in the brief rather than granting access to outside source or answer keys.
16|
17|The committed `experiments/NN-<slug>/brief.md` names the export path, charter, relevant skill, this protocol, budget, permission profile and acceptance checks. It states the export-only reading rule and contains no information about what is planted. The coordinator supplies the charter; it is not assembled by the explorer from the plan.
18|
19|## Before the probe
20|
21|Each charter has one target, named resources/instruments and one kind of information:
22|
23|```text
24|Explore <target> with <resources> to discover <information>.
25|I predict <observable behavior>.
26|Source: <spec line, code file:line, model cell, previous surprise or risk hypothesis>.
27|I would be wrong if <observable refutation>.
28|Budget: 60 minutes wall clock; planned reading / probing / writing split.
29|```
30|
31|Write predictions and refutation conditions before executing the corresponding probe, including new hypotheses formed mid-run. A source reading is evidence for a prediction, not its confirmation. Separate should (named oracle), predicted (what code appears to do) and observed (what ran). Later observations can shape the next probe within this charter. Backlog adjacent questions as `#offcharter`; the explorer never widens the assignment.
32|
33|The run budget includes reading, probing, resetting and writing. Track elapsed time and the actual reading/probing/writing split. No probe is worth losing the record to a time-out.
34|
35|## During the run
36|
37|Keep `experiments/NN-<slug>/notes.md` as timestamped entries. Use UTC timestamps and these tags:
38|
39|| Tag | Record |
40||---|---|
41|| `#read` | Source observation with file:line and its interpretation |
42|| `#hypothesis` | Id, source, prediction and refutation before the probe |
43|| `#obs` | Exact command, trimmed output and observed effects |
44|| `#surprise` | A discrepancy requiring characterization |
45|| `#bug` | Evidence and report link for an oracle violation |
46|| `#question` | An unresolved question or missing observation |
47|| `#offcharter` | Adjacent lead saved without expanding the target |
48|
49|Retain dead ends, failed commands and timestamps. Trim repetitive output but retain evidence that determines the judgment. Preserve raw output or a linked artifact when trimming would lose meaning. Record fixture/reset identity, actors and relevant clock state. Read-only database observations are permitted; inject failures through lab/partner controls, container actions or documented clock controls, not hidden service paths or ad hoc source changes.
50|
51|When no console answers a question, record a testability request with the question, missing signal, minimal hook and validation probe. The explorer proposes hooks; the fixer implements them in the separate fix stage.
52|
53|## Characterize surprises
54|
55|Every `#surprise` ends in a defect report or an explicit written reason it is not one. Isolate variables and reduce the reproduction. If it will not reproduce, preserve exact original state, vary one thing at a time, suspect timing and clock sources, and keep attempts and uncertainty in the log.
56|
57|Reports under `defects/` contain:
58|
59|- Title and tag/build seen at; link to the original observation.
60|- Exact minimal setup and steps, including actor, clock and fixture assumptions.
61|- Expected behavior with its named oracle: spec line, Never/Always rule, comparable system/standard or approximation with bounds.
62|- Observed behavior and evidence.
63|- Variables isolated, including what did not matter.
64|- Sibling check: where else the same cause could live, with file:line, or “none found.” Predictions about siblings must precede their probes.
65|- Severity with impact, and status: `open`, `fixed in lesson NN`, `won't fix: <why>` or `spec`.
66|
67|The explorer writes reports in its own words with local provisional identifiers if necessary. The coordinator reconciles them with the hidden register: retain the planted `D##` id when matched; assign `U##` to an unplanned finding. Identifier reconciliation must not insert the register’s explanation into the explorer’s account.
68|
69|## Close and score the run
70|
71|Write `revealed.md` with charter status (`done`, `needs more` or `blocked`), elapsed time and reading/probing/writing split, what the system showed in plain words, model delta with file/cell links, unresolved uncertainties and next hypotheses. End with this score table, using actual counts and evidence links:
72|
73|| Measure | Count | Evidence / counting basis |
74||---|---|---|
75|| Hypotheses stated | | Distinct ids stated before probing |
76|| Hypotheses confirmed | | Predictions supported by the stated observation |
77|| Hypotheses refuted | | Stated refutation condition observed |
78|| Code-reading predictions contradicted by the running system | | Refuted subset whose recorded source was code |
79|| Defects found | | Distinct evidenced reports, excluding disclosure |
80|| Model cells filled | | Previously unobserved cells now supported by evidence |
81|
82|Record hypotheses left `needs more` explicitly; confirmed plus refuted need not equal stated. Neither running a command nor adding an inferred diagram cell establishes observed coverage. Count a repeated observation once, and link separate defect findings even when one probe exposes several. A prediction of a defect can be confirmed while the product behavior violates its oracle; keep these judgments separate.
83|
84|An experiment may need a second run with a narrowed charter. It closes after at most two runs. The coordinator discloses remaining planted misses in the lesson note under “What the experiment missed, and why,” and the fixer flags them `disclosed`. Never backfill these into the explorer’s notes, scores or finds. Preserve out-of-order and unplanned discoveries as they happened.
85|
86|## Backlog and living models
87|
88|`hypotheses.md` retains every proposed hypothesis: id, statement/prediction, source, refutation, intended probe/experiment and status (`open` or `experiment NN: confirmed|refuted|needs more`). Keep original statements when updating outcomes.
89|
90|Models under `models/` grow from observations: `map.md`, `nouns-verbs.md`, `variables.md`, `rules.md`, `entities.md`, `states.md`, `ecosystem.md` and, after evidence supports cause analysis, `causes.md`. Label inference and uncertainty. Later experiments revise earlier models; their diffs are evidence of learning. In a cause-prediction run, commit or timestamp the predicted-defects table before running the confirming probes.
91|
92|## Handoff and verification
93|
94|The coordinator commits experiment artifacts as produced, formatting only. Fixes belong in a separate fresh fixer run from the seeder’s family, using the reports as brief. The fixer changes only named findings, adds a regression check per defect under `project/test/checks/` and black-box repro scripts under `project/lab/repro/`, and writes the lesson note. A spec silence also needs a spec line and the coordinator’s one-line decision in the fix commit body. The lesson tag points at the fix commit. Fix history remains separate from the experiment record.
95|
96|`make verify LESSON=NN` resets and runs that experiment’s repros and checks. Its final verdict is `FIXED AND CHECKED:` after repair or `DEFECTS REPRODUCED:` against the earlier version. Repros report `PRESENT:` or `ABSENT:` per defect; thresholds are binary and may not be weakened to hide a defect. `REF=<tag>` uses the current repros against earlier SUT code. `make checks` runs all regression checks; `make test` runs unit tests. `make dwell LESSON=NN` optionally shows present/absent across earlier tags; its result does not gate the verdict. Lesson 00 uses `BASELINE HOLDS:`.
97|
98|Lesson notes include actual found/missed/found-early/unplanned outcomes, the score and before/after evidence. Review checks that previous-version repros still reproduce the finding, models match evidence and no answer key leaked into the brief or export.
99|
100|## Source and local adaptations
101|
102|Hendrickson, [*Explore It!*](https://pragprog.com/titles/ehxta/explore-it/) (2013): 1.1–1.3, 2.1–2.4 and 2.6, Chapter 3, 10.4, 11.5–11.6 and 13.3. Section numbering checked against the publisher’s contents extract; detailed text review remains pending. Blind exports, split agent roles, explicit prediction/refutation lines, score format and the two-commit lesson are this repo’s implementation of the approved plan, not claims of prescribed book formats.

59|- Title and tag/build seen at; link to the original observation.
60|- Exact minimal setup and steps, including actor, clock and fixture assumptions.
61|- Expected behavior with its named oracle: spec line, Never/Always rule, comparable system/standard or approximation with bounds.
62|- Observed behavior and evidence.
63|- Variables isolated, including what did not matter.
64|- Sibling check: where else the same cause could live, with file:line, or “none found.” Predictions about siblings must precede their probes.
65|- Severity with impact, and status: `open`, `fixed in lesson NN`, `won't fix: <why>` or `spec`.
66|
67|The explorer writes reports in its own words with local provisional identifiers if necessary. The coordinator reconciles them with the hidden register: retain the planted `D##` id when matched; assign `U##` to an unplanned finding. Identifier reconciliation must not insert the register’s explanation into the explorer’s account.
68|
69|## Close and score the run
70|
71|Write `revealed.md` with charter status (`done`, `needs more` or `blocked`), elapsed time and reading/probing/writing split, what the system showed in plain words, model delta with file/cell links, unresolved uncertainties and next hypotheses. End with this score table, using actual counts and evidence links:
72|
73|| Measure | Count | Evidence / counting basis |
74||---|---|---|
75|| Hypotheses stated | | Distinct ids stated before probing |
76|| Hypotheses confirmed | | Predictions supported by the stated observation |
77|| Hypotheses refuted | | Stated refutation condition observed |
78|| Code-reading predictions contradicted by the running system | | Refuted subset whose recorded source was code |
79|| Defects found | | Distinct evidenced reports, excluding disclosure |
80|| Model cells filled | | Previously unobserved cells now supported by evidence |
81|
82|Record hypotheses left `needs more` explicitly; confirmed plus refuted need not equal stated. Neither running a command nor adding an inferred diagram cell establishes observed coverage. Count a repeated observation once, and link separate defect findings even when one probe exposes several. A prediction of a defect can be confirmed while the product behavior violates its oracle; keep these judgments separate.
83|
84|An experiment may need a second run with a narrowed charter. It closes after at most two runs. The coordinator discloses remaining planted misses in the lesson note under “What the experiment missed, and why,” and the fixer flags them `disclosed`. Never backfill these into the explorer’s notes, scores or finds. Preserve out-of-order and unplanned discoveries as they happened.
85|
86|## Backlog and living models
87|
88|`hypotheses.md` retains every proposed hypothesis: id, statement/prediction, source, refutation, intended probe/experiment and status (`open` or `experiment NN: confirmed|refuted|needs more`). Keep original statements when updating outcomes.
89|
90|Models under `models/` grow from observations: `map.md`, `nouns-verbs.md`, `variables.md`, `rules.md`, `entities.md`, `states.md`, `ecosystem.md` and, after evidence supports cause analysis, `causes.md`. Label inference and uncertainty. Later experiments revise earlier models; their diffs are evidence of learning. In a cause-prediction run, commit or timestamp the predicted-defects table before running the confirming probes.
91|
92|## Handoff and verification
93|
94|The coordinator commits experiment artifacts as produced, formatting only. Fixes belong in a separate fresh fixer run from the seeder’s family, using the reports as brief. The fixer changes only named findings, adds a regression check per defect under `project/test/checks/` and black-box repro scripts under `project/lab/repro/`, and writes the lesson note. A spec silence also needs a spec line and the coordinator’s one-line decision in the fix commit body. The lesson tag points at the fix commit. Fix history remains separate from the experiment record.
95|
96|`make verify LESSON=NN` resets and runs that experiment’s repros and checks. Its final verdict is `FIXED AND CHECKED:` after repair or `DEFECTS REPRODUCED:` against the earlier version. Repros report `PRESENT:` or `ABSENT:` per defect; thresholds are binary and may not be weakened to hide a defect. `REF=<tag>` uses the current repros against earlier SUT code. `make checks` runs all regression checks; `make test` runs unit tests. `make dwell LESSON=NN` optionally shows present/absent across earlier tags; its result does not gate the verdict. Lesson 00 uses `BASELINE HOLDS:`.
97|
98|Lesson notes include actual found/missed/found-early/unplanned outcomes, the score and before/after evidence. Review checks that previous-version repros still reproduce the finding, models match evidence and no answer key leaked into the brief or export.
99|
100|## Source and local adaptations
101|
102|Hendrickson, [*Explore It!*](https://pragprog.com/titles/ehxta/explore-it/) (2013): 1.1–1.3, 2.1–2.4 and 2.6, Chapter 3, 10.4, 11.5–11.6 and 13.3. Section numbering checked against the publisher’s contents extract; detailed text review remains pending. Blind exports, split agent roles, explicit prediction/refutation lines, score format and the two-commit lesson are this repo’s implementation of the approved plan, not claims of prescribed book formats.

+## The focused patch and decisions
+
+- `objectPayload` in `internal/api/enqueue.go` is the existing enqueue rule factored out for
+  schedule creation. Omission becomes `{}`; explicit null and other JSON types are rejected.
+  No payload PATCH field is added. Existing manual/cron execution consumes validated templates.
+- `deleteSchedule` checks RowsAffected and returns service-owned schedule_not_found for zero.
+- Client JSON decoding and qctl option/output decoding use `UseNumber`. The worker's existing
+  sleep/failure numeric consumers accept json.Number, retaining their omitted-value defaults.
+  The baseline lease check parses its returned ID as exact int64 and retains its priority and
+  concurrent-disjoint-lease assertions.
+- Ack recursively checks result strings and object keys for NUL; nack checks error text.
+  Both return 400 invalid_result/invalid_error before touching lease, attempts or result.
+- `missingQueue` recognizes only the assigned owner foreign-key violations, returning 404
+  queue_not_found without schema text. Enqueue, batch, manual schedule run and schedule create
+  use that mapping. No speculative lease-race repair is included.
+- `migrations/005.sql` adds `attempts_job_owner ON DELETE CASCADE` and a job-id index. It is
+  NOT VALID so existing legacy orphans remain inspectable; it enforces new writes and removes
+  attempts when their existing owner subsequently leaves. This fix does not bulk-delete old
+  orphan evidence or alter independent outbox/events lifetimes.
+- Retention selects succeeded/cancelled, exempting dead.

+retries or explicitly deletes them; automatic retention applies only to succeeded/cancelled**

+(U33 / Q-E06-2 attempts half). Schedule payloads use the existing enqueue contract; NUL result/error
+is a 400 with a valid lease left usable. Delivered-outbox cleanup stays undecided.

+# 06 — Relate it: owners, dependents and the data's journey
+
+An entity diagram suggests two useful questions: what happens when an owner disappears,
+and does a value survive every path that carries it? Here, queue deletion already refused
+while jobs or schedules existed. Following payloads beyond the API found different answers:
+the API preserved numbers, but queuelet's CLI and sample worker rounded them. Following a
+job through deletion found attempt rows that no API could reach afterwards.
+
+The sources are Hendrickson, *Explore It!* (2013), Chapter 7.1 “Recognizing Entities,
+Attributes, and Dependencies”, 7.2 “CRUD”, and 7.3 “Following the Data”. These are
+[approved-plan citations](../PLAN.md#22-chapter-map-kept-sections-only), checked against
+the chapter map, not a claim of full-text validation by this fixer.
+
+## What the blind experiment learned
+
+The [original record](../exploration/experiments/06-relate-it/revealed.md) belongs to
+exploration commit `b3b0559`. It is preserved byte-for-byte, including its reports, tools,
+models and score. The fresh Claude explorer used about 20 minutes of its 60-minute budget:
+roughly 3 reading, 10 probing and 7 writing. This fresh Codex Sol fix follows the coordinator's
+[assignment](../register/reconciliations/06.md); it is not another exploration run.
+
+| Original measure | Actual score |
+|---|---:|
+| Hypotheses stated | 20 |
+| Confirmed | 18 |
+| Refuted | 2 |
+| Code-reading predictions contradicted, as recorded | 2 |
+| Reports | 7 |
+| Observed model cells | 30 |
+
+The two contradictions need their original qualifications. H-E06-C predicted owner
+orphans from the original schema; reading migration 002 had already counter-predicted the
+queue guard before the probe confirmed it. H-E06-17 predicted a batch race error that did
+not occur in 320 tries. That sampling non-hit does not prove the window absent. The
+explorer explicitly reported no new contradiction of its own deterministic code predictions.
+
+| Classification | Actual outcome |
+|---|---|
+| Expected here, found early | D15 queue deletion orphans dependents, D16 schedule edits keep an old next fire, D17 webhook truncation: found and fixed in E01. D08 numeric loss at the API and D27 disabled firing were also repaired early. They are not rediscoveries here |
+| Found in E06 | Seven unplanned reports, reconciled to U27–U33 below; all fixed, none deferred |
+| Missed / disclosed planted defects | None remain to disclose |
+| Spec silence, resolved here | A4 dead-job retention, a coordinator policy decision. The explorer observed succeeded/cancelled retention, did not probe dead retention and filed no A4 report |
+
+The plan's teaching prediction changed. E06 did not newly expose D15–D17 or show different
+queue/schedule orphan behavior. The repaired queue guards and snapshot rules held. The
+useful distinction became **which dependencies should share a lifetime**, and **which
+client decoder lies between two otherwise exact storage boundaries**.
+
+## The seven faults, at `explore-it/lesson-05`
+
+Paths below are relative to `project/` in that tag, not line numbers in the repaired tree.
+
+| ID | Original report | Previous-tag source | Observable failure |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| U27 | [E06-F01](../exploration/defects/E06-F01-schedule-delete-missing-204.md) | `internal/api/schedules.go:136` | DELETE missing/repeated/foreign schedule says 204 even when no row changed |
+| U28 | [E06-F02](../exploration/defects/E06-F02-schedule-payload-not-validated.md) | `internal/api/schedules.go:55`, `internal/schedule/fire.go:76`; compare `internal/api/enqueue.go:64` | template accepts null/non-objects, cron copies them into jobs, manual run rejects them; omitted payload becomes null |
+| U29 | [E06-F03](../exploration/defects/E06-F03-sample-worker-echo-loses-precision.md) | `internal/client/client.go:57`, `internal/worker/worker.go:79` | worker decodes numbers as float64; echo result and webhook contain the rounded value |
+| U30 | [E06-F04](../exploration/defects/E06-F04-qctl-rounds-payload-numbers.md) | `cmd/qctl/main.go:52`, `cmd/qctl/main.go:277` | enqueue input is rounded before storage; job get rounds exact stored payload and result for display |
+| U31 | [E06-F05](../exploration/defects/E06-F05-nul-in-result-or-error-409-conflict.md) | `internal/api/jobs.go:65`, `internal/api/jobs.go:88` | NUL in result/error causes PostgreSQL rejection reported as 409 state_conflict with driver text, while lease remains valid |
+| U32 | [E06-F06](../exploration/defects/E06-F06-enqueue-racing-queue-delete-400-fk-text.md) | `internal/api/enqueue.go:88`, `internal/api/schedules.go:57` | owner disappears between lookup and insert: 400 invalid_job or 500 database_error with constraint text instead of 404 |

+
+A4 lived in `internal/jobs/expire.go:91`: the sweep included dead alongside succeeded and
+cancelled. That was consistent with the then-silent policy, not an eighth blind defect.
+
+## CRUD before and after
+
+“Before” is the explorer's observed lesson-05 grid in
+[entities.md](../exploration/models/entities.md#crud-grid-entity--operation-observed-in-e06-unless-marked).
+“After” describes this repair's direct checks and the unchanged observations explicitly
+labelled below. Worker read/update cells without an API remain unobserved. The pre-E06 model was
+also narrower: its original entity rows still said queue→job/schedule had no FK,
+and attempt deletion had no observed outcome. E06 adds the repaired FK/guard table,
+observes each job-removal path and separates the outbox/event lifetime. The model
+file retains those dated revisions rather than overwriting what was believed earlier.
+
+| Entity | Create before → after | Read before → after | Update before → after | Delete before → after |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| Queue | race loser leaks FK → 404 queue_not_found | namespace ownership holds → unchanged | max-attempt and notification snapshots hold → unchanged | dependent guard holds → race controls still refuse 409, empty delete 204 |
+| Job | qctl rounds → exact payload; race 400 → 404 | qctl rounds payload/result → exact display | NUL ack/nack 409 → service-owned 400, valid lease untouched and clean retry succeeds | terminal delete removes job only → job and attempts leave; events and pending notifications remain |
+| Schedule | non-object/null accepted, omission null → non-object/null rejected, omission {}; race 500 → 404 | missing GET 404 → still 404 | cron/zone/enabled rules already repaired → unchanged; PATCH still refuses payload | missing/foreign/repeated 204 → 404, real delete 204 |
+| Worker | registers → isolated worker still registers and processes | no new read observation | no new update observation | release counted; process may keep polling deleted id → unchanged, recovery question deferred |
+| Attempt | completion records it → one real row before each deletion test | orphan visible only in storage → live job's attempt remains reachable | no update API | never removed → removed on job DELETE, purge and retention |
+| Outbox | terminal snapshot → exact worker result snapshot | signed partner bytes preserve API values → worker values now exact too | delivery retries → pending snapshots still deliver after job deletion | independent lifetime → unchanged; delivered-row cleanup remains open |
+| Job event | transitions recorded → unchanged | survives job removal → checked through API and real storage | no mutation API | independent lifetime → unchanged |
+
+Automatic job deletion adds a policy distinction: dead persists; succeeded/cancelled age
+out. It is tested with a frozen API clock below cutoff and beyond two sweep opportunities,
+with API status and SELECT counts agreeing. Retained dead work can still be retried.
+
+## Follow payload, result and error
+
+| Datum / hop | Before | After / evidence |
+|---|---|---|
+| Payload: HTTP enqueue → jsonb → API/lease | exact values; jsonb normalizes form | exact API control still holds; normalization of key order, whitespace and `1e2` is not value loss |
+| Payload: qctl --payload → API → jsonb | float64 rounding | direct write/read check preserves `9007199254740993`, a long fractional decimal and a nested 64-bit integer |
+| Payload: schedule create → stored template → manual/cron job | incompatible validation; cron admitted poison payloads | same object/default contract; both paths produce equivalent valid values; PATCH gains no field |
+| Payload → worker decode → echo result | numbers rounded inside client | target container's worker produces exact result; sleep and fail numeric consumers still work |
+| Result: ack → jsonb → outbox → partner | API exact; worker already rounded it upstream | exact worker result reaches partner with valid signature; API and webhook values agree |
+| Result: qctl --result/--json and job get | shared float decoder | ack, batch and schedule JSON sibling paths checked directly; exact API-written payload/result displayed exactly |
+| Error/result: NUL → storage | PG rejects it; service calls it state_conflict | reject before mutation, including nested strings and object keys; literal backslash-u text stays valid |
+| Error: nack → attempt/history → job removal | attempt error text outlives inaccessible job | attempts share job lifetime; events and pending terminal snapshots keep independent lifetime |
+
+## The focused patch and decisions
+
+- `objectPayload` in `internal/api/enqueue.go` is the existing enqueue rule factored out for
+  schedule creation. Omission becomes `{}`; explicit null and other JSON types are rejected.
+  No payload PATCH field is added. Existing manual/cron execution consumes validated templates.
+- `deleteSchedule` checks RowsAffected and returns service-owned schedule_not_found for zero.
+- Client JSON decoding and qctl option/output decoding use `UseNumber`. The worker's existing
+  sleep/failure numeric consumers accept json.Number, retaining their omitted-value defaults.
+  The baseline lease check parses its returned ID as exact int64 and retains its priority and
+  concurrent-disjoint-lease assertions.
+- Ack recursively checks result strings and object keys for NUL; nack checks error text.

+# E06: checking data boundaries and dependent lifetimes
+
+Project-specific findings from experiment 06 and its repair; VM facts belong elsewhere.
+
+- Exact storage does not imply exact clients. Check CLI input against storage and CLI output
+  against a separately API-written value. A single CLI round trip can hide symmetric corruption.
+  Use a large integer, a long fractional decimal and a nested value; parse observations without
+  binary floating-point conversion. `lab/repro/probe06.py` supplies the public E06 checks.
+- REF must run target-image qctl and worker binaries. Current instrument code is appropriate;
+  current application decoding is not. Starting a target-image worker on a unique queue makes
+  its data path observable without changing the service or colliding with seeded workers.
+- A decoder change to json.Number also changes numeric consumers: sleep/failure controls need
+  to keep working, including omitted-field defaults. Preserve both the data and the behavior. Tests consuming
+  the shared client must parse IDs as json.Number/Int64 rather than assuming float64; retain
+  their behavioral assertions. E06 preserves the failed baseline run and repeats the entire
+  paired sequence after this test-consumer adaptation.
+- Deleting an owner has several independent effects. Check actual storage, API reachability,
+  durable events and pending delivery completion. API 404 alone cannot establish storage cleanup.
+  Attempts now follow their job; events and notification snapshots retain independent lifetimes.
+- Retention needs both a preserved class and deleted controls. Freeze API time, observe below
+  cutoff, advance past it, bound real waits for sweeps, then inspect real rows. Do not substitute
+  a projected count or SQL-mutated fixture for storage evidence.
+- The API reruns migration SQL on every startup. Constraint additions need the same catalog guard
+  as existing migrations. The first E06 rebuild exposed a missing guard; its log and diagnostics
+  are preserved, and repeated startups during reset/acceptance exercise the repair.
+- A sampled race non-hit is not proof that its window is absent. Require the actual reported
+  historical errors for the paired claim. Current checks also need successful/missing-owner
+  controls, exact accepted-row cardinality, known error codes and no orphaned writes.
+
+No reusable VM helper or knowledge-store write was warranted. The E06 oracle is indexed in
+`project/lab/repro/README.md`; the acceptance launcher remained scratch under `/tmp`.
+- Hooksink's `body` convenience field is itself parsed through float64. Precision assertions
+  must decode `raw_body`, the original received bytes, using Decimal/integer parsing. E06's
+  first current attempt failed explicitly on this measurement error; the corrected instrument
+  is frozen identically for both final verification directions. The sink is unchanged.

+# E06: checking data boundaries and dependent lifetimes
+
+Project-specific findings from experiment 06 and its repair; VM facts belong elsewhere.
+
+- Exact storage does not imply exact clients. Check CLI input against storage and CLI output
+  against a separately API-written value. A single CLI round trip can hide symmetric corruption.
+  Use a large integer, a long fractional decimal and a nested value; parse observations without
+  binary floating-point conversion. `lab/repro/probe06.py` supplies the public E06 checks.
+- REF must run target-image qctl and worker binaries. Current instrument code is appropriate;
+  current application decoding is not. Starting a target-image worker on a unique queue makes
+  its data path observable without changing the service or colliding with seeded workers.
+- A decoder change to json.Number also changes numeric consumers: sleep/failure controls need
+  to keep working, including omitted-field defaults. Preserve both the data and the behavior. Tests consuming
+  the shared client must parse IDs as json.Number/Int64 rather than assuming float64; retain
+  their behavioral assertions. E06 preserves the failed baseline run and repeats the entire
+  paired sequence after this test-consumer adaptation.
+- Deleting an owner has several independent effects. Check actual storage, API reachability,
+  durable events and pending delivery completion. API 404 alone cannot establish storage cleanup.
+  Attempts now follow their job; events and notification snapshots retain independent lifetimes.
+- Retention needs both a preserved class and deleted controls. Freeze API time, observe below
+  cutoff, advance past it, bound real waits for sweeps, then inspect real rows. Do not substitute
+  a projected count or SQL-mutated fixture for storage evidence.
+- The API reruns migration SQL on every startup. Constraint additions need the same catalog guard
+  as existing migrations. The first E06 rebuild exposed a missing guard; its log and diagnostics
+  are preserved, and repeated startups during reset/acceptance exercise the repair.
+- A sampled race non-hit is not proof that its window is absent. Require the actual reported
+  historical errors for the paired claim. Current checks also need successful/missing-owner
+  controls, exact accepted-row cardinality, known error codes and no orphaned writes.
+
+No reusable VM helper or knowledge-store write was warranted. The E06 oracle is indexed in
+`project/lab/repro/README.md`; the acceptance launcher remained scratch under `/tmp`.
+- Hooksink's `body` convenience field is itself parsed through float64. Precision assertions
+  must decode `raw_body`, the original received bytes, using Decimal/integer parsing. E06's
+  first current attempt failed explicitly on this measurement error; the corrected instrument
+  is frozen identically for both final verification directions. The sink is unchanged.

 `DELETE /v1/jobs/{id}` removes a terminal job.
+Attempt records belong to their job and are removed with it on deletion, purge and
+automatic retention; durable job events and pending webhook snapshots keep their independent lifetime.
 Only a `leased` job has a lease token, holder and expiry; every exit from
 `leased` clears all three; attempt rows keep the worker that ran them.
 
@@ -106,6 +108,8 @@ Only the current lease holder may complete or extend a job. A lease ends at its
 `lease_expires_at`: from that instant heartbeat, ack and nack are 409, whether or
 not the background loop has released the job yet. There is no grace period.
 Ack moves a leased job to `succeeded`.
+A result containing U+0000 (including object keys), or an error containing U+0000,
+is 400 `invalid_result` or `invalid_error`; the valid lease remains usable.
 Nack with retry moves a job to `retry_wait`; when due it becomes `queued`.
 A failed job reaches `dead` when its maximum attempts are exhausted, or when
 nacked with retry false. No job may execute more than its maximum attempts.
@@ -119,7 +123,8 @@ A cancelled job is never run.
 `POST /v1/jobs/{id}/retry` permits an operator to retry a dead job, resets its
 attempt count and makes it immediately available.
 Succeeded and cancelled jobs cannot be retried.
-Terminal jobs are deleted after `retention_hours`.
+Succeeded and cancelled jobs are deleted after `retention_hours`.
+Dead jobs remain until an operator retries or explicitly deletes them; automatic retention exempts them.
 The API returns complete stored results and errors.
 
 ## Schedules
@@ -129,6 +134,8 @@ Cron uses five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week.
 Time zones use IANA identifiers, defaulting to UTC.
 Schedule times follow the named zone's local civil time, including offset changes.
 The enabled flag defaults to true; disabled schedules do not enqueue jobs.
+Schedule creation follows enqueue's payload rule: omitted means `{}`, explicit null
+and non-object values are invalid. PATCH does not accept payload.
 `GET /v1/schedules` lists schedules; `GET /v1/schedules/{id}` reads one.
 `PATCH /v1/schedules/{id}` updates cron, timezone or enabled status; the next fire
 must reflect the current configuration.

1|# E06-F03 — The sample worker rounds payload numbers: `echo` returns 9007199254740992 for 9007199254740993 and 1.1 for 1.10
2|
3|Seen at: export of `explore-it/lesson-05` (stack `queuelet-e06`), experiment 06 (relate-it).
4|Original observation: [E06 notes](../experiments/06-relate-it/notes.md) P4, 15:35:24Z (H-E06-05, predicted from code).
5|Prior record: D08 (lesson 01) fixed API-side precision and left "client-side qctl/worker numeric loss" as an unprobed
6|prediction; this is its first observation.
7|
8|## Minimal reproduction
9|
10|Actor: acme key; worker-b (sample worker, documented kinds) serves `reports`, which has a webhook to hooksink.
11|Clock: real.
12|
13|```sh
14|source exploration/experiments/06-relate-it/tools/env.sh
15|k acme-key POST /v1/queues/reports/jobs '{"kind":"echo","priority":9,"payload":{"big":9007199254740993,"dec":1.10}}'
16|sleep 6
17|sql "select payload::text, result::text from jobs where id=<id>"
18|curl -s $QUEUELET_HOOK_URL/admin/records | jq -r '.records[].raw_body'
19|```
20|Replay: `tools/p4-journey.sh` (job A).
21|
22|## Expected (named oracle)
23|
24|README "Echo returns its payload"; SPEC:63 "Payload values are delivered to workers without loss of numeric
25|precision". The worker shipped with queuelet (`cmd/worker`, `qctl worker run`) is the documented consumer; echo's
26|result should be value-equal to the payload. A control job acked by hand with the same numbers (job 311) shows the
27|API, storage and webhook keep the digits, so the loss is attributable to the worker alone.
28|
29|## Observed
30|
31|| Hop | Value of `big` / `dec` |
32||---|---|
33|| request | 9007199254740993 / 1.10 |
34|| psql `jobs.payload`, `GET /v1/jobs`, lease bytes | 9007199254740993 / 1.10 |
35|| psql `jobs.result` (after worker-b's echo) | **9007199254740992 / 1.1** |
36|| outbox body, hooksink raw_body (signature valid) | **9007199254740992 / 1.1** |
37|| control job 311, manual ack | 9007199254740993 / 1.10 everywhere |
38|
39|## Variables isolated
40|
41|- Matters: the job passes through `internal/client.Client.JSON` (`client.go:57`, `json.Unmarshal` without `UseNumber`)
42|  into `worker.Job.Payload map[string]any` (`worker.go:21`), i.e. float64.
43|- Does not matter: queue, webhook, priority. Integers ≤ 2^53 and decimals without trailing zeros survive.
44|
45|## Sibling search
46|
47|- `worker.go:82, :88` (`sleep`, `fail`) read float64 from the same map — only affects values beyond 2^53, harmless.
48|- `worker.go:98-110` `http` kind: response decoded with `json.Unmarshal` into `any` → same loss for remote results.
49|- `cmd/qctl` uses the same pattern for input and output → separate report [E06-F04](E06-F04-qctl-rounds-payload-numbers.md).
50|- Server side: lease (`jobs.go:81` RawMessage), GET (`store.go` RawMessage), ack (`api.go:53-62` UseNumber), Notify and
51|  Ship (RawMessage) — exact (P4 control).
52|
53|## Severity and status
54|
55|Severity: **low–medium**. Large ids (e.g. 64-bit database keys or snowflake ids) in payloads come back altered from the
56|reference worker and are notified to partners altered, with a valid signature. Status: **open**.

1|# E06-F04 — qctl rounds numbers both ways: `enqueue --payload` stores a different number, and `job get` displays one
2|
3|Seen at: export of `explore-it/lesson-05` (stack `queuelet-e06`), experiment 06 (relate-it).
4|Original observation: [E06 notes](../experiments/06-relate-it/notes.md) P5, 15:36:13Z (H-E06-14, H-E06-15, predicted
5|from code; sibling of [E06-F03](E06-F03-sample-worker-echo-loses-precision.md)).
6|
7|## Minimal reproduction
8|
9|Actor: acme key; qctl binary from the e06 image (run inside the api container against `http://localhost:8200`).
10|
11|```sh
12|source exploration/experiments/06-relate-it/tools/env.sh
13|q() { docker exec -e QUEUELET_URL=http://localhost:8200 -e QUEUELET_KEY=acme-key queuelet-e06-api-1 qctl "$@"; }
14|q enqueue reports --kind manual --payload '{"big":9007199254740993,"dec":1.10}'   # {"id": 312, "state": "queued"}
15|sql "select payload::text from jobs where id=312"     # {"big": 9007199254740992, "dec": 1.1}
16|k acme-key POST /v1/queues/reports/jobs '{"kind":"manual","payload":{"big":9007199254740993,"dec":1.10}}'   # control, id 313
17|sql "select payload::text from jobs where id=313"     # {"big": 9007199254740993, "dec": 1.10}
18|q job get 311      # stored 9007199254740993 / 1.10, printed "big": 9007199254740992, "dec": 1.1
19|```
20|Replay: `tools/p5-qctl.sh`.
21|
22|## Expected (named oracle)
23|
24|README: "The CLI and the HTTP API expose the same operations." SPEC:63 numeric precision. The same body sent by curl
25|is stored exactly (job 313), so the CLI must not change the data it sends, and its display must show the stored value.
26|
27|## Observed
28|
29|- Input: `qctl enqueue … --payload` stored `9007199254740992` / `1.1` (job 312).
30|- Output: `qctl job get 311` printed `9007199254740992` / `1.1` for a row whose payload and result hold
31|  `9007199254740993` / `1.10`.
32|
33|## Variables isolated
34|
35|- Matters: `cmd/qctl/main.go:52-57` `jsonOpt` decodes every `--payload`/`--result`/`--json` option into `any`
36|  (float64) before re-encoding; `main.go:277-280` decodes every response into `any` before `MarshalIndent`.
37|- Does not matter: endpoint, queue, kind. Values ≤ 2^53 without trailing zeros are unaffected.
38|- `jsonOpt` also ignores parse errors (an invalid `--payload` becomes `null`) — the API then rejects it (400), so no
39|  corrupt write results; noted, not counted.
40|
41|## Sibling search
42|
43|All qctl verbs share `jsonOpt` and the printer: `ack --result`, `batch --json`, `schedule create --json`,
44|`queue create/patch --json` (predicted same loss; not probed individually). Worker client: E06-F03.
45|
46|## Severity and status
47|
48|Severity: **medium** for the write path (an operator using the documented CLI silently enqueues different data than
49|typed), **low** for display. One report because one decoding habit causes both. Status: **open**.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
lesson=${1:-00}
if [[ -n ${REF:-} && ${QUEUELET_REF_ACTIVE:-0} != 1 ]]; then
  root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
  scratch=$(mktemp -d /tmp/queuelet-ref.XXXXXX)
  original_project=$PWD
  target="$scratch/books/explore-it/project"
  cleanup_ref() {
    status=$?
    trap - EXIT
    set +e
    if ((status != 0)); then
      mkdir -p "$original_project/results"
      diagnostics=$(mktemp -d "$original_project/results/ref-failure.XXXXXX")
      if [[ -n $diagnostics ]]; then
        printf 'REF=%s\nlesson=%s\nexit_status=%s\n' "$REF" "$lesson" "$status" > "$diagnostics/run.txt"
        docker compose -f "$target/deploy/compose.yml" ps -a > "$diagnostics/compose-ps.log" 2>&1
        docker compose -f "$target/deploy/compose.yml" logs --no-color > "$diagnostics/compose.log" 2>&1
        printf 'REF verification failed (exit %s); diagnostics: %s\n' "$status" "$diagnostics" >&2
      else
        echo 'Could not create REF diagnostics directory; dumping Compose state to stderr' >&2
        docker compose -f "$target/deploy/compose.yml" ps -a >&2
        docker compose -f "$target/deploy/compose.yml" logs --no-color >&2
      fi
    fi
    docker compose -f "$target/deploy/compose.yml" down -v >/dev/null 2>&1
    rm -rf "$scratch"
    exit "$status"
  }
  trap cleanup_ref EXIT
  git -C "$root" archive "$REF" books/explore-it/project | tar -x -C "$scratch"
  export COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=queuelet-ref QUEUELET_API_PORT=18210 QUEUELET_HOOK_PORT=18211 QUEUELET_PG_PORT=15443 QUEUELET_IMAGE_TAG=ref
  export QUEUELET_URL=http://localhost:18210 QUEUELET_HOOK_URL=http://localhost:18211 QUEUELET_REF_ACTIVE=1
  docker compose -f "$target/deploy/compose.yml" up -d --build
  bash lab/wait.sh
  # Run current instruments against the historical binaries.
  cp -R lab/. "$target/lab/"
  mkdir -p "$target/test/checks"
  cp -R test/checks/. "$target/test/checks/"
  (cd "$target"; REF="$REF" bash lab/verify.sh "$lesson")
  exit $?
fi
if [[ $lesson == 00 ]]; then
  bash lab/reset.sh
  go test ./...
  go test -tags checks ./test/checks -run L00 -count=1
  echo 'BASELINE HOLDS: enqueue→lease→ack→webhook; unit and happy-path checks pass'
  exit 0
fi
# Each fixer adds an ids file and immutable black-box repro scripts with its lesson.
idsfile="lab/repro/lesson-$lesson.ids"
[[ -f $idsfile ]] || { echo "No reproductions registered for lesson $lesson" >&2; exit 2; }
bash lab/reset.sh
present=0; absent=0
mapfile -t ids < "$idsfile"
expected=${#ids[@]}
((expected > 0)) || { echo "PROBE ERROR: empty reproduction list" >&2; exit 2; }
declare -A seen=()
for id in "${ids[@]}"; do
  [[ $id =~ ^([DU][0-9]{2}|[AT][0-9]+)$ ]] || { echo "PROBE ERROR: invalid reproduction ID $id" >&2; exit 2; }
  [[ ! -v seen[$id] ]] || { echo "PROBE ERROR: duplicate reproduction ID $id" >&2; exit 2; }
  seen[$id]=1
  result=$(bash "lab/repro/$id.sh" </dev/null)
  printf '%s\n' "$result"
  if [[ $result == "PRESENT: $id — "* ]]; then ((present+=1)); elif [[ $result == "ABSENT: $id — "* ]]; then ((absent+=1)); else echo "PROBE ERROR: invalid verdict for $id" >&2; exit 2; fi
done
[[ $((present+absent)) == "$expected" ]] || exit 2
if [[ -n ${REF:-} ]]; then
  if [[ ${QUEUELET_DWELL:-0} == 1 ]]; then
    echo "DWELL: $present present; $absent absent"
    exit 0
  fi
  [[ $absent == 0 ]] || { echo 'Historical reproduction incomplete' >&2; exit 1; }
  echo "DEFECTS REPRODUCED: $present present"
else
  [[ $present == 0 ]] || { echo "VERIFICATION FAILED: $present present; $absent absent" >&2; exit 1; }
  go test -tags checks ./test/checks -run "L$lesson" -count=1
  echo "FIXED AND CHECKED: $absent absent; regression checks pass"
fi
